name: Templeton Emerging Markets Investment Trust plc
company_name: Templeton Emerging Markets Investment Trust plc
overview: Templeton Emerging Markets Investment Trust plc (‘TEMIT’) is a UK-domiciled, London-listed closed-end investment trust launched in June 1989 that invests in a concentrated, actively managed portfolio of emerging-markets equities, aiming for long-term capital appreciation. It is managed by Franklin Templeton's Templeton Global Investments (TGI) team, led by Chetan Sehgal and Andrew Ness, and has total net assets of £2,525.6 million as at 31 March 2026 (FY2026). Shares trade on the London Stock Exchange (primary listing, ~245.5p at 31 March 2026) and on the NZX under TEM.NZ (secondary listing, NZD-quoted, same underlying share, much thinner liquidity).

business_model.summary: TEMIT is not an operating company — it is a closed-end fund. It generates shareholder returns through three levers: (1) growth in Net Asset Value (NAV) as its emerging-markets equity portfolio appreciates, (2) a rising ordinary dividend paid from portfolio income, and (3) narrowing (or widening) of the discount between the share price and NAV per share, which mechanically adds to or subtracts from total shareholder return independent of NAV performance. The Company has no employees; all functions (portfolio management, AIFM/company secretary, depositary/custody, marketing) are outsourced to Franklin Templeton entities and third parties.

revenue_streams.name: Capital appreciation of listed EM equity portfolio (NAV growth)
revenue_streams.trend: primary return driver; NAV total return +41.3% in FY2026 vs +8.8% FY2025

revenue_streams.name: Portfolio dividend/investment income funding shareholder distributions
revenue_streams.trend: stable; total income £65.6m in FY2026 (2025: £70.4m), revenue earnings 5.39p/share

revenue_streams.name: Covered call option premiums (new, authorised Sept 2025)

business_model.customer_type: Retail and institutional shareholders (UK-majority register, with NZ secondary-listing holders); not a customer-facing operating business
business_model.geographic_mix: Portfolio by country as at 31 March 2026: China/Hong Kong 23.4% (benchmark 25.5%, underweight), Taiwan 23.0% (benchmark 22.5%, overweight), South Korea 22.0% (benchmark 15.5%, overweight), Brazil 9.5% (benchmark 5.1%, overweight), India 8.5% (benchmark 12.6%, underweight; 10.5% including indirect exposure via Genpact/Cognizant), South Africa 3.1%, Mexico 2.5%, United States (EM-revenue names) 2.0%, Thailand 1.3%, Hungary 1.1%, Chile 1.1%, others ~2%.

fee_structure.management_fee: AIFM fee to be phased down from 1 July 2026 to 1.0% on the first £1bn of net assets and 0.5% on the excess — a blended rate of just under 0.7% at year-end NAV levels
fee_structure.note: OCR decline reflects both the fee-rate cut and a higher average NAV base over the year

business_model.dividend: Total ordinary dividend 5.25p for FY2026 (unchanged vs FY2025: 2.00p interim + 3.25p final), fully covered by revenue earnings of 5.39p/share. Board commitment is to at least maintain 5.00p/year despite the mandate being capital-growth, not income, focused; dividend is a discount-narrowing / shareholder-friendly commitment rather than the core value proposition.

portfolio_positioning.top_10_concentration: Top 10 holdings typically account for over 45% of the portfolio (portfolio construction house style); ~47.7% at 31 March 2026 per the disclosed weights
sector_overweights: Information Technology (semiconductor/AI supply chain — TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, MediaTek)
sector_underweights: Financials (though still large in absolute terms)
largest_active_country_bets: Overweight South Korea (+6.5pp vs benchmark) — semiconductors/memory, EV/robotics via Hyundai, corporate governance reform tailwind
Overweight Brazil (+4.4pp) — rate-cut cycle, Petrobras, Itaú, Banorte-style domestic financials
Underweight China/Hong Kong (-2.1pp) — selective, concentrated in internet platforms and industrials, cautious on structural demographics
Underweight India (-4.1pp headline, -2.1pp including indirect exposure) — valuation discipline despite favourable long-term structural story
portfolio_positioning.portfolio_style: High-conviction, bottom-up, low-turnover (typically <20% p.a.) stock picker; country/sector weights are a residual of stock selection, not top-down calls. 50-100 stock portfolio, max 12% single-issuer limit. Not index-hugging — meaningful concentration in AI/semiconductor supply chain names.

performance_record.assessment: FY2026 was an exceptional outperformance year (+15.4pp vs benchmark, driven by stock selection +9.8pp, sector allocation +4.9pp, currency +0.7pp, and buyback impact +0.8pp), largely from an overweight in AI/semiconductor beneficiaries (SK Hynix, TSMC) and South Korea generally. However, the 5-year record is materially weaker in absolute and relative terms: +38.2% NAV cumulative vs +25.4% benchmark (only ~12.8pp of cumulative outperformance over 5 years, and FY2022 was a -17.3% NAV year during the 2022 EM/China drawdown). Investors should not extrapolate the FY2026 headline number; the trust's edge has been real but lumpy, concentrated in strong recent stock calls rather than a smooth compounding pattern.
performance_record.discount_history: Year-end discount to NAV: 15.4% (FY2024) → 12.4% (FY2025) → 8.2% (FY2026); further at 8.9% as at 21 May 2026 (latest practicable date in the Annual Report) and reported around 8.0% by Edison Group's research note covering H1 FY2027 (six months to 30 Sept 2025, NAV TR +25.3% vs benchmark +18.8%).

main_competitors: JPMorgan Emerging Markets Growth & Income (formerly JPMorgan Emerging Markets Investment Trust)
Schroder Asian Total Return / other regional EM/Asia specialist trusts
competitive_position.market_position: TEMIT is the largest and one of the longest-track-record UK-listed global emerging markets investment trusts, with net assets of £2.5 billion at FY2026 year end and a market capitalisation reported around £2.2-2.9 billion through 2026. Independent research (Edison Group) ranks TEMIT first among its closest peers (Fidelity Emerging Markets, JPMorgan EM Growth & Income) over 5- and 10-year NAV total return.

moat_factors.description: Franklin Templeton's Templeton Global Investments team has 100+ analysts/PMs across 17 countries with average 18+ years' experience, research coverage of 1,200+ companies (700+ in EM), and multi-decade on-the-ground presence since TEMIT's 1989 launch — a genuine informational edge in less-covered EM names.
As the largest UK-listed EM trust, TEMIT has better secondary-market liquidity and lower relative running costs than smaller peers, though this advantage does not extend to the NZX line.

36+ years of history, AAA Citywire rating for lead managers (May 2025), multiple AIC marketing awards; brand recognition among UK retail investors is a genuine distribution advantage versus newer or smaller vehicles.

Fixed capital base means the managers are not forced to sell into EM illiquidity during redemption waves (unlike open-ended EM funds), allowing genuine long-term, low-turnover (<20% p.a.) positioning in less liquid names.

OCR of 0.86% (falling toward ~0.7% blended from July 2026 fee cut) is competitive within actively managed EM closed-end funds and below some smaller peers, but is a clear cost disadvantage versus passive EM ETFs (which typically charge 0.07%-0.20%).

weaknesses: No moat versus a low-cost EM index ETF for an investor who just wants EM beta — TEMIT must continually prove manager alpha net of fees to justify the wrapper

Persistent, structural discount to NAV (averaged 9.7% over FY2026, still 8-9% at latest disclosure) shows the market has not historically been willing to pay full NAV for the trust, eroding part of the manager's NAV outperformance

High-conviction, concentrated portfolio (top 10 >45%) with heavy semiconductor/AI supply-chain exposure (TSMC + SK Hynix + Samsung Electronics + MediaTek alone are >30% of the portfolio) means TEMIT's recent outperformance is largely a single-theme bet rather than diversified stock-picking skill across sectors
5-year and 10-year relative outperformance versus benchmark, while positive, is modest once the exceptional FY2026 year is excluded

growth_drivers: EM equities trade at a substantial valuation discount to developed markets, and management/Board argue the 'Magnificent 7' alone are worth more than the entire MSCI EM Index — a re-rating catalyst if capital rotates away from US mega-cap concentration
AI-driven capex cycle benefiting TEMIT's large semiconductor/memory overweights (TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics) in Taiwan and South Korea

Board's active discount-narrowing programme: £166.7m of buybacks in FY2026 (avg 10.2% discount, adding 0.8% to NAV/share) and a stated intent to repurchase up to £300m over the next 12-24 months (up from £200m previously)
AIFM fee cut effective 1 July 2026 (1.0% on first £1bn, 0.5% above, blended ~0.7%) directly improves the OCR and net return to shareholders
Conditional Tender Offer: if 5-year NAV total return to March 2029 fails to beat the benchmark, the Board must offer to buy back up to 25% of shares near NAV — a shareholder-aligned discount backstop
Continued rising ordinary dividend (5.25p FY2026, minimum commitment of 5.00p) supporting a total-return case for income-oriented holders
Structural EM growth narrative: EM economies represent ~half of world GDP and ~65% of global economic growth per IMF/WEF data cited by the Board
South Korea corporate governance reforms (Commercial Act amendments, 'Value-Up' programme) improving shareholder returns and potentially re-rating Korean holdings
Brazil rate-cutting cycle (commenced March 2026) supporting domestic equities and reducing the appeal of competing fixed income

business.description: 23.4% of portfolio in China/HK; structural headwinds include a shrinking, ageing population, a weakening anti-involution campaign, and internet-platform AI capex pressuring near-term free cash flow.

TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics and MediaTek together represent roughly a third of the portfolio; a reversal in the AI capex cycle or memory pricing would disproportionately hit NAV given this is also where most of FY2026's outperformance came from.
Bottom-up, high-conviction stock selection (not index-hugging) means periods of sentiment-driven, non-fundamental markets can see TEMIT materially underperform, as occurred in FY2022 (-17.3% NAV).
LUKOIL and Sberbank of Russia remain on the books at fair value of zero (trading suspended); an eventual write-up (or permanent write-off confirmation) is an open, low-probability tail item.

financial.description: New £122m multi-currency revolving credit facility (GBP/USD/CNH) drawn to ~1.2% net gearing at FY2026 year-end; modest but amplifies both gains and losses, and CNH drawings add a further currency dimension.

TEMIT does not hedge currency risk; portfolio companies are priced in local EM currencies, TEMIT reports and pays dividends in GBP, and the NZX line is quoted in NZD — a NZ holder carries local-currency/GBP risk (embedded in NAV) plus GBP/NZD risk (on top, via the quoted price) simultaneously.
0.86% OCR (falling toward ~0.7%) is a permanent headwind versus a passive EM ETF at a fraction of the cost; must be overcome by manager alpha every year.

regulatory.description: Dual FCA (LSE) and NZX regulatory regimes increase compliance complexity, though the Board states its risk framework is designed to manage this.

Sanctions, capital controls, tax changes or trade restrictions in any investee country could impair income, valuation or marketability of holdings (explicitly flagged as a principal risk in the FY2026 Annual Report).

Even though the US Supreme Court struck down the 'Liberation Day' tariffs in Feb 2026 (reverting to a 10% baseline), US-China friction, technology export controls and the Taiwan Strait situation remain live and directly relevant given TEMIT's ~46% combined China/HK + Taiwan exposure.

macro.description: TEMIT is a leveraged-to-EM-sentiment vehicle; a broad EM selloff (as in FY2022, -17.3% NAV) hits both NAV and typically widens the discount simultaneously, compounding losses for shareholders.

macro.risk: Middle East conflict / oil price shock
macro.description: US-Israel strikes on Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption in Feb-March 2026 already dented NAV late in FY2026; continued Middle East escalation raises energy costs for oil-importing EMs (Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines, India) and could further pressure inflation and margins.

Even with active buybacks, the Board itself calls the historical persistence and scale of the discount 'unsatisfactory'; a return to double-digit discounts (as recently as FY2024's 15.4%) would erode share-price returns independent of NAV performance.

execution.description: Performance is significantly dependent on lead PM Chetan Sehgal and Andrew Ness; the Company explicitly flags Key Personnel as a principal risk, mitigated only by Franklin Templeton's succession planning.

execution.risk: Continuation vote / Conditional Tender Offer overhang
execution.description: Next 5-yearly continuation vote is 2029 AGM (2024 vote passed 99.3% in favour, so near-term risk is low); however the Conditional Tender Offer (up to 25% of shares near NAV if 5-yr NAV TR to March 2029 underperforms benchmark) creates a defined, dated performance test the managers must clear.
David Graham retiring at the 2026 AGM after 9 years; a new Non-Executive Director is being recruited. Routine trust-governance turnover, not a red flag on its own.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Emerging markets equities are in a period of renewed relative interest as US mega-cap valuations (especially the 'Magnificent 7') look stretched; EM represents about half of global GDP and ~65% of global growth (IMF/WEF), a structural underweight versus most global index/portfolio allocations. AI capex remains the dominant near-term thematic driver, concentrated in Taiwan/Korea semiconductor supply chains.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High. EM equities are a high-beta, sentiment-sensitive asset class; TEMIT's NAV total return ranged from -17.3% (FY2022) to +41.3% (FY2026) in the last five fiscal years, illustrating the swings investors must tolerate.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate/indirect — EM equity valuations and currencies are sensitive to US dollar strength and global rate cycles; several key EM markets (Brazil, India) are in domestic easing cycles that are a portfolio tailwind, while a stronger-for-longer US dollar or renewed Fed hawkishness would be a headwind.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Portfolio holdings are priced in Taiwan dollar, Korean won, Chinese yuan/HK dollar, Brazilian real, Indian rupee, Mexican peso, and other EM currencies; NAV and dividends are reported/paid in GBP; the NZX line trades in NZD. TEMIT does not hedge currency risk at the portfolio level.
key_input_costs: Portfolio management/AIFM fee (falling to a blended ~0.7% from 1 July 2026)
Broker/marketing costs (significant annual marketing budget matched by Franklin Templeton)

nzx_listing_specifics.structure: TEM.NZ is a secondary NZX listing of the same ordinary shares that trade as TEM on the London Stock Exchange; there is one class of share and one global NAV, but two separate trading venues and currencies.
nzx_listing_specifics.liquidity: The vast majority of TEMIT's shareholder base and trading volume is in London; the NZX line is materially thinner. The FY2026 Annual Report and half-yearly reports repeat verbatim that 'while the majority of the Company's shareholders are based in the UK, shares are traded on both the London and New Zealand stock exchanges,' with the Board's discount-management commentary (buybacks, stockbroker discount monitoring 'at the close of each trading day in London') focused on the London line.
nzx_listing_specifics.price_risk: Because the NZX line is thinner, its quoted price can lag or diverge from the London price and NAV, especially around GBP/NZD FX moves or when London-driven news breaks outside NZX trading hours; NZ holders should expect wider effective spreads and potential temporary premium/discount dislocation versus the London-quoted discount to NAV (8.2% at 31 March 2026, ~8.9% at 21 May 2026).
nzx_listing_specifics.fx_layer: An NZ holder is exposed to: (1) EM local-currency moves embedded in the GBP NAV, (2) GBP itself (since NAV/dividends are GBP-denominated), and (3) GBP/NZD translation on top, since the NZX price and any NZD dividend conversion add a third currency layer versus a UK holder.
nzx_listing_specifics.disclosure: TEMIT publishes NZX-specific announcements (NAV updates, half-year and annual results, board notices) directly via the NZX Market Announcement Platform in parallel with LSE RNS releases, so NZ holders have the same disclosure timeliness as UK holders, but liquidity/execution risk sits on top of that.

recent_developments.event: FY2026 Annual Results (year to 31 March 2026): NAV total return +41.3% vs benchmark +26.8%; net assets £2,525.6m; discount narrowed to 8.2% at year end; OCR fell to 0.86%; full-year dividend maintained at 5.25p per share, fully covered by revenue earnings of 5.39p; £166.7m spent on buybacks during the year.
Latest practicable discount to NAV disclosed in the Annual Report was 8.9%, showing some re-widening from the 8.2% year-end print.
Death of Dr. Mark Mobius, TEMIT's founder and 'father of emerging markets investing,' noted in memoriam in the FY2026 Annual Report.

US Supreme Court ruled Trump-era 'Liberation Day' tariffs unconstitutional; a 10% baseline tariff rate was implemented across the board from end-February 2026, reducing (but not eliminating) trade-policy uncertainty for the remainder of TEMIT's fiscal year.

Coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran and the resulting Strait of Hormuz disruption drove a late-period sell-off in EM markets and a decline in TEMIT's NAV in March 2026, tempering (but not reversing) the year's strong return.

TEMIT renewed its revolving credit facility, entering a new £122m multi-currency (GBP/USD/CNH) facility with The Bank of Nova Scotia, replacing the fixed-term loan that matured/was repaid January 2025; interim dividend of 2.00p paid 30 January 2026.

Board authorised the Investment Managers to use covered call options and equity CFDs to manage geared equity exposure more flexibly and potentially at lower cost; minor investment-policy changes made without requiring shareholder approval. Research teams of Franklin Templeton Emerging Markets and Templeton Global Equity Group were fully integrated under Templeton Global Investments (TGI) effective September 2025.
Half-Yearly Results to 30 September 2025: NAV total return +25.3% vs benchmark +18.8% for the six months; share price total return +30.8%; interim dividend held at 2.00p.
Lead managers Chetan Sehgal and Andrew Ness awarded Citywire's highest AAA rating for consistent long-term performance managing TEMIT.

David Graham to retire from the Board at the July 2026 AGM after nine years' tenure; recruitment of a new Non-Executive Director underway. AGM to be livestreamed for the first time, with guest speaker Jeff Prestridge (financial journalist).

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report (2 June 2026) and H1 FY2027 Half-Yearly Report (30 September 2025 period)

items.target: At least 5.00p per share per year
items.notes: FY2026 actual dividend of 5.25p was above this floor and fully covered by revenue earnings; no guarantee of maintenance from year to year per the stated distribution policy, but the Board has consistently paid above the 5.00p floor since committing to it two years ago.

items.target: Up to £300 million over the next 12-24 months
items.period: From FY2026 year-end (increased from a prior £200m commitment)
items.notes: Reflects the increased market capitalisation of the Company; buybacks executed at an average 10.2% discount in FY2026, adding 0.8% to remaining shareholders' NAV per share.

items.target: 1.0% on first £1bn of net assets, 0.5% on the excess (blended just under 0.7% at FY2026 year-end NAV)
items.notes: Phased fee reduction announced as part of the Board's broader package (alongside dividend floor, buybacks, and Conditional Tender Offer) to improve shareholder returns and narrow the discount.

items.target: Tender for up to 25% of issued share capital at NAV less 2% (less costs) if 5-year cumulative NAV total return underperforms the MSCI EM benchmark
items.period: Measurement period 31 March 2024 to 31 March 2029; tender (if triggered) would follow the 2029 AGM
items.notes: No new guidance issued in FY2026; performance to date (cumulative NAV TR well ahead of benchmark over the period so far) makes triggering the tender look unlikely on current trend, but the mechanism remains in force through March 2029.

Driven by the AIFM fee cut effective 1 July 2026 plus any further growth in average net assets; not an explicit point-estimate guidance figure but a direct mechanical consequence of the announced fee schedule.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Angus Macpherson reiterated that the Board does not believe buybacks alone will eliminate the discount; closing it durably requires (1) renewed investor enthusiasm for EM equities, (2) investment performance that makes TEMIT structurally attractive versus alternatives, and (3) continued marketing to broaden the shareholder base. Portfolio Managers Sehgal and Ness reaffirmed conviction in AI/semiconductor supply-chain exposure (Taiwan, South Korea), selective Chinese internet and industrial names, Brazil's rate-cutting cycle, and a cautiously constructive, still-underweight stance on India pending clearer visibility on tariff and AI-disruption effects on IT-services-linked names.

bull_case: Exceptional FY2026 NAV outperformance (+41.3% vs benchmark +26.8%) demonstrates the manager's stock-picking edge is real when fundamentals (rather than macro sentiment) drive EM returns, particularly in the AI/semiconductor supply chain

Discount to NAV has narrowed sharply (15.4% → 12.4% → 8.2% over the last three fiscal years) and the Board is actively closing it further via an enlarged £300m buyback programme, a falling fee schedule (blended ~0.7% from July 2026), and a Conditional Tender Offer backstop — all mechanically additive to shareholder total return independent of NAV

Structural re-rating case for EM equities versus historically stretched US mega-cap valuations, with EM representing about half of world GDP and ~65% of global growth but a much smaller share of global index weightings and investor allocations

Largest, longest-track-record UK-listed global EM trust, ranked first among its closest peers (Fidelity EM, JPMorgan EM Growth & Income) over 5- and 10-year NAV total return per independent research, backed by Franklin Templeton's 100+ analyst EM research platform
Rising, fully-covered ordinary dividend (5.25p FY2026, floor of 5.00p) provides a modest income underpin on top of the primary capital-growth thesis
bear_case: 5- and 10-year NAV outperformance versus benchmark is much more modest once the exceptional FY2026 year is excluded, and FY2022 (-17.3% NAV) shows the drawdown risk is real and can coincide with discount widening, compounding losses

Portfolio is heavily concentrated in a single AI/semiconductor supply-chain theme (TSMC + SK Hynix + Samsung Electronics + MediaTek alone >30% of the portfolio); a reversal in AI capex sentiment or memory pricing would hit both absolute NAV and relative performance simultaneously

Discount to NAV, while narrowed, remains persistent (8-9%) and the Board itself calls its historical scale 'unsatisfactory'; buybacks alone have not eliminated it and a return to double-digit discounts would erode share-price total returns even if NAV performance stays strong

Elevated and intensifying geopolitical risk directly relevant to ~46% combined China/HK + Taiwan exposure — US-China trade/tech tensions, Taiwan Strait risk, and broader Middle East conflict spillover into oil prices and EM currencies

A simple, unhedged low-cost EM index ETF is a genuine substitute for investors who just want EM beta, at a fraction of TEMIT's ~0.86% (falling to ~0.7%) ongoing charges, without discount/NAV divergence risk or NZX-specific liquidity/FX layering for NZ holders
